title: bk export — emit a vectorizable bead corpus
description:
# bk export — emit a vectorizable bead corpus

## Summary

Add a `bk export` subcommand that emits a normalized, curated, indexable
representation of beads across one or more projects, designed to be fed into
ANY vector store (ToolGate vector, pgvector, etc.). Beekeeper does NOT embed,
index, or own a vector — it only produces a clean corpus. The vector layer
lives outside the binary (a separate `bkx`/ToolGate-app consumer).

## Why bk is the right tap (vs reading raw beads/issues from GitHub)

A naive indexer pointed straight at `issues.jsonl` on a repo's default branch
gets a raw, possibly-stale, per-repo, un-normalized, noisy view. `bk` already
does the work that makes the corpus correct and high-signal:

1. Authoritative / de-drifted state — bead state lives on a sync branch; trunk
   holds stale copies and feature branches strand writes. `bk` (trunk-sync /
   drift logic) knows where the reconciled truth is, so the export reflects the
   CURRENT state, not "whatever is on main".
2. Cross-project aggregation + identity normalization — walks all `.beads/`
   hives and canonicalizes drifted actor handles.
3. Resolved cross-bead relationships — dependency graph (blocks/blocked-by),
   lease/assignee state, supersession links — computed across beads, absent
   from any single raw issue.
4. Stable schema across `bd` versions — one consistent output shape so the
   indexer writes no per-source glue.
5. Curation — classify routine vs decision/data-bearing beads so the index is
   high-signal (the biggest quality lever for a knowledge/decision index).

## Command

    bk export [paths...] [flags]

Walks the given paths (default: cwd) for `.beads/` projects, same discovery as
`bk doctor` / `bk board`. Read-only; never mutates beads, never shells out to
mutate `bd`.

## Output

- One document per bead. Default format NDJSON (one JSON object per line) for
  streaming into ingest pipelines; `--format json` for a single array.
- Stable, documented schema (below). Deterministic field ordering.

### Document schema (per bead)

- `id` — bead id (e.g. `bkg-9cs`). Stable; use as the vector `source_uri` for
  idempotent overwrite-on-change.
- `repo` — originating project (path or repo slug).
- `title`
- `body` — issue description.
- `comments` — flattened comment thread (the richest rationale signal),
  optionally concatenated into `text` (see flags).
- `text` — assembled embedding payload (title + body + comments per flags).
- `status`, `issue_type`, `priority`, `labels`, `assignee`.
- `deps` — resolved `{blocks: [...], blocked_by: [...]}`.
- `created_at`, `updated_at`, `closed_at`.
- Computed curation metadata:
  - `is_routine` (bool) — heuristic: short body, no rationale language, chore/
    typo/bump-style.
  - `is_decision` (bool) — label-driven first (`decision`/`adr`/`architecture`),
    text-signal fallback ("because", "decided", "rejected", "instead of").
  - `richness` (number) — body+comment length / signal score.
  - `superseded_by` — bead id(s) that reverse/replace this one, when derivable
    from links.

Classification is emitted as METADATA FLAGS, never as deletion — the indexer or
the query decides what to filter. Keeps the export a faithful projection
(consistent with the "owns no issue data" tenet) and lets the caller change
their mind at query time.

## Tuning parameters (the fine-tuning the export should expose)

- `--format ndjson|json` (default ndjson).
- `--output PATH` / stdout default.
- `--status open|closed|all` (default all).
- `--type feature,task,...` / `--labels a,b` — include/exclude filters.
- `--since DATE` — only beads updated after DATE (incremental re-index).
- `--include-comments` (default true) / `--no-comments`.
- `--include-closed` (default true) — closed beads are valuable as prior art for
  decision retrieval.
- `--classify` (default true) — compute `is_routine`/`is_decision`/`richness`.
- `--min-richness N` — drop low-signal beads below a threshold (off by default;
  prefer flags over deletion).
- `--decisions-only` — convenience filter to `is_decision=true`.
- `--text-template` — control how `text` is assembled (e.g.
  `"{{title}}\n\n{{body}}\n\n{{comments}}"`).
- `--fields a,b,c` — project a subset of schema fields.
- `--repo-filter GLOB` — restrict to matching projects (cross-project tap).
- `--redact` — optional scrub of emails/tokens from text.

Classification heuristics MUST be configurable (label-driven first, text/length
fallback) and documented as a ranking aid, not ground truth.

## Non-goals (scope guard)

- No embedding, no vector index, no server inside `bk`. Keeps the
  single-static-binary, zero-dependency, no-server properties intact.
- No new source of truth — export is a derived, rebuildable projection of the
  JSONL, exactly like the SQLite cache.
- The vector consumer (`bkx` / ToolGate app + sync job) is a SEPARATE work item.

## Acceptance criteria

- `bk export` discovers `.beads/` across given paths and emits one document per
  bead in NDJSON (default) and JSON.
- Output reflects authoritative/reconciled bead state (not stale trunk copies)
  and normalized actor identities.
- Schema includes title/body/comments/status/type/labels/assignee/deps/
  timestamps + `is_routine`/`is_decision`/`richness`/`superseded_by`.
- All tuning flags above implemented with sensible defaults; `--since` enables
  incremental re-index; `--decisions-only` and `--min-richness` filter signal.
- Deterministic output (stable ordering) so re-runs diff cleanly.
- Read-only: never mutates beads/JSONL, never touches the daemon.
- Unit tests for schema, filters, classification heuristics, and
  authoritative-state selection.
- README documents the command, schema, and flags.

## Cross-platform release (must ship like the rest of bk)

- Built and released for macOS, Linux, and Windows via the existing goreleaser
  pipeline.
- Homebrew tap (`brew install theaichimera/tap/bk`) updated on release.
- Windows `.zip` asset in the GitHub release.
- Version bump + changelog entry; docs-only `docs:` excluded from changelog as
  configured.

## Open questions

- Should `text` assembly default to including comments, or make it opt-in for
  cost? (Leaning: include by default — comments carry the rationale.)
- Supersession links: derivable from existing dep types, or need a new link
  kind in `bd`?
- Where does `bk export` draw the authoritative-state line for a dirty working
  tree / unsynced sync branch — warn, or refuse, or export-as-of-sync-branch?
close_reason: completed in 384e3da

title: Rationale + progressions as schema-driven bead artifacts (beadspec + bk enforcement)
description:
# Rationale + progressions as schema-driven bead artifacts (beadspec + bk enforcement)

## Summary
Establish two first-class, distinct knowledge artifacts on top of beads, and make Beekeeper (bk) enforce their structure from a **declarative schema** instead of hard-coded Go rules.

- **Rationale** — per-decision justification, authored at epic-creation time, stored inside the epic. Static, decision-scoped, frozen.
- **Progression** — topic-scoped, longitudinal narrative (where we started, pivots, current understanding). A dedicated `progression`-labeled bead with a maintained `## Current understanding` header + an append-only dated `## Log`. Living, self-correcting, kept OFF the work board.

The schema that defines these shapes lives in a new leaf package **`pkg/beadspec`** inside this repo. bk's `doctor` and `hooks` consume beadspec and become schema-driven.

## Background / motivation
Audit of the legacy `~/.claude/knowledge` progressions library (2026-06-05) showed automatic capture has lapsed:
- agentflow: no progression documents since 2026-05-13 despite heavy activity.
- Most projects hold only the one-time `00_codebase-analysis.md` baseline.
- `/reflect`'s synthesized `current_position` is empty on 11 of 17 agentflow progressions.

The dormant high-value features (ambient auto-injection, `/reflect` synthesis) aren't worth maintaining a second library for. Consolidate onto beads (already in the daily loop: bk board, git-synced, GitHub-visible). The legacy library is retained read-only; no migration.

## The two artifacts (model)

### Rationale (lives in the epic)
- Authored at epic creation, next to the "what".
- Captured as a `## Decisions` section; every entry is `Decision: <what> — Why: <rationale>`.
- Frozen: it records the reason at decision time; it is not corrected over time.

### Progression (its own bead)
- A `progression`-labeled bead, NOT owned by a single epic (a progression spans many epics/PRs).
- Body shape:
  - `## Current understanding` — a maintained synthesis (the "where we are now").
  - `## Log` — append-only, dated, typed entries: `baseline | deepening | pivot | correction`.
  - Links to the epics/PRs it spans.
- Lifecycle is active → concluded (parked), never "done" like work.
- Excluded from `bk board` / ready queue.

## Decisions
- Decision: Keep rationale and progressions as TWO distinct artifacts — Why: different temporality/scope. Rationale is point-in-time + decision-local + frozen; a progression is longitudinal + topic-scoped + self-correcting. Collapsing them loses the pivot/current-understanding arc.
- Decision: Rationale lives inside the epic, authored at creation — Why: the "why this choice" is freshest at decision time and belongs beside the what.
- Decision: A progression is its own `progression`-labeled bead, not owned by one epic — Why: progressions span multiple epics/PRs; binding to a single epic is wrong.
- Decision: Do NOT wrap `bd create` as `bk create` — Why: highest-maintenance chokepoint (Go + brew release lag); `bd create --label` already suffices; enforcement belongs in doctor+hooks, which catch beads regardless of who created them.
- Decision: bk owns deterministic structure + validation; the agent owns content authoring — Why: a CLI can scaffold a skeleton but cannot write meaningful rationale/narrative; baking prose into Go makes iteration painful.
- Decision: Enforce as hook (hard block at push) + doctor (cross-project visibility); never block `bd create` — Why: matches existing land-the-plane discipline; stub epics must be creatable mid-thought.
- Decision: Tooling enforces presence + shape only; completeness/quality is a review gate (human or advisory LLM) — Why: a linter cannot detect an omitted decision or judge whether a Why is meaningful; a blocking judgment gate trains gaming.
- Decision: Progressions excluded from `bk board` / ready queue — Why: living docs aren't actionable work.
- Decision: beadspec is a leaf `pkg/` package, NOT a new repo; promote to its own repo only on a 2nd independent consumer — Why: separation of concerns without the solo-maintainer two-repo release tax. Constraint: beadspec imports nothing from bk; bk imports beadspec (one-way), so future extraction is a folder move.
- Decision: Build in beekeeper-go; keep legacy `~/.claude/knowledge` progressions read-only — Why: it's a bk capability; no big-bang migration.

## Architecture
```
pkg/beadspec/                 # NEW leaf package (public, importable)
  doc.go                      # schema-format documentation
  schema.go                   # types + loader for the DSL
  schemas/epic.yaml           # seed: rationale + ## Decisions rules
  schemas/progression.yaml    # seed: ## Current understanding + label + log
  validate.go                 # pure validation: (bead, schema) -> []Finding
internal/doctor/   -> imports pkg/beadspec, runs Validate over beads
internal/hooks/    -> imports pkg/beadspec, pre-push gate
internal/board/    -> excludes `progression` label from ready/board
cmd/bk/progression.go         # NEW scaffolder command (new/add/list)
```
Dependency direction is one-way: **bk → beadspec**. beadspec has zero bk imports.

## Children
- `.1` beadspec: schema DSL/format + `pkg/beadspec` skeleton + pure validator
- `.2` beadspec: seed schemas for `epic` + `progression`
- `.3` bk `doctor`: schema-driven lint (consumes beadspec)
- `.4` `bk progression` scaffolder (new/add/list)
- `.5` bk `board`/ready: exclude `progression` label
- `.6` bk `hooks`: pre-push enforcement (reuses .3 validation)
- `.7` downstream: adopt convention in consuming repos' AGENTS.md (agentflow first)

## Out of scope (now)
- Ambient auto-injection of progression current-understanding into agent context (dormant; possible future `bk progression show` session-start nudge).
- Advisory LLM rationale-quality check (separate future bead).
- Migration of legacy `~/.claude/knowledge` progressions (kept read-only).

## Acceptance
- `pkg/beadspec` defines a declarative schema format with seed schemas for `epic` + `progression`, unit-tested, zero imports from bk.
- `bk doctor` flags — from the schema, not hard-coded — epics with empty rationale / malformed `## Decisions` entries (missing `Why`) / progression beads missing `## Current understanding` or the `progression` label.
- `bk progression new|add|list` scaffolds and maintains a beadspec-conforming progression bead, parked off the board.
- `bk board` and ready views exclude `progression`-labeled beads.
- Pre-push hook blocks landing an epic that violates the epic schema, reusing the same beadspec validation.

title: beadspec: schema DSL/format + pkg/beadspec skeleton + pure validator
description:
# beadspec: schema DSL/format + pkg/beadspec skeleton + pure validator

## Summary
Create the new leaf package `pkg/beadspec` that declaratively defines bead structure ("bead types and their required shape"), plus a pure validation function. This is the DSL the rest of the epic builds on.

**Hard constraint:** NO bk imports. One-way dependency `bk → beadspec`, so the package can be extracted to its own repo later by moving the folder.

## Scope
- New package `pkg/beadspec/` (public, under `pkg/` so it is externally importable).
- Define the **schema format**. A schema describes, per bead type:
  - required body sections (markdown headers, e.g. `## Decisions`)
  - required labels (e.g. `progression`)
  - field rules (e.g. `description`/`design` non-empty)
  - per-section item rules (e.g. each bullet under `## Decisions` must contain `Why:`)
- Format: YAML, shipped via `go:embed` under `schemas/`.
- Go types: `Schema`, `SectionRule`, `LabelRule`, `ItemRule`, `Finding`.
- `func Validate(bead Bead, schema Schema) []Finding` — pure, deterministic, **presence + shape only**. No I/O, no bk deps.
- `func Load(beadType string) (Schema, error)` — load embedded schema by bead type.
- A minimal `Bead` view type (id, type, labels, body/description) so beadspec does not depend on bk's bead model.
- Table-driven unit tests for the validator.

## Acceptance
- `pkg/beadspec` compiles as a leaf package with **zero imports** from `internal/*` or `cmd/*` (add a guard test asserting this).
- Schema format documented in `doc.go`.
- `Validate` covered by table-driven tests: a passing case + one case per failure mode.
- New bead types can be added by dropping a YAML schema — no Go changes required.

## Deps
- None. Foundational.
close_reason: Shipped: pkg/beadspec schema DSL + pure validator + leaf guard test.

title: beadspec: seed schemas for epic + progression
description:
# beadspec: seed schemas for epic + progression

## Summary
Author the two seed schema definitions consumed by doctor, hooks, and the scaffolder. These are the concrete, authoritative shape definitions for the two artifacts in the parent epic.

## Scope
- `schemas/epic.yaml`:
  - require non-empty `description`/`design` (rationale present)
  - require a `## Decisions` section
  - each `## Decisions` entry must contain a `Why:` (accept `— Why:` / `Why:`), i.e. every decision paired with rationale
- `schemas/progression.yaml`:
  - require label `progression`
  - require non-empty `## Current understanding` section
  - require `## Log` section
  - log entries should be dated (validate a leading `YYYY-MM-DD` on each log item if cheap; otherwise shape-only)
- Golden example beads (conforming) for use in tests.

## Acceptance
- `beadspec.Load("epic")` and `beadspec.Load("progression")` both load.
- A conforming example passes `Validate`.
- Representative violations each produce the expected `Finding`:
  - epic missing `## Decisions`
  - a decision entry without `Why:`
  - progression missing `## Current understanding`
  - progression missing the `progression` label

## Deps
- Blocked by `.1` (schema format must exist first).
close_reason: Shipped: seed schemas epic.toml + progression.toml with golden tests.

title: bk doctor: schema-driven rationale/progression lint
description:
# bk doctor: schema-driven rationale/progression lint

## Summary
Make `bk doctor` consume `pkg/beadspec` and emit findings for beads that violate their type's schema. This replaces hard-coded rule constants with schema-driven checks — bk becomes the engine, beadspec is the source of truth.

## Scope
- In `internal/doctor`, for each bead: resolve its schema by type (`epic`, `progression`, ...), run `beadspec.Validate`, and surface findings in the existing doctor output format.
- Findings to surface: epic missing rationale; `## Decisions` entry missing `Why`; progression missing `## Current understanding`; progression missing the `progression` label.
- Respect existing doctor noise-suppression / worktree-dedup behavior (cf. `bkg-x25`).
- Runs cross-project (doctor already does).

## Acceptance
- `bk doctor` reports the above violations against real beads, sourced **from beadspec schemas** (no hard-coded rule constants in doctor).
- Existing doctor tests still pass.
- New wiring tests cover the beadspec path (`internal/doctor` → `pkg/beadspec`).

## Deps
- Blocked by `.1` and `.2`.
close_reason: Shipped: bk doctor schema-driven bead-schema check via internal/beadlint.

title: bk progression: scaffolder command (new/add/list)
description:
# bk progression: scaffolder command (new/add/list)

## Summary
Add `cmd/bk/progression.go` implementing a scaffolder for progression beads that conform to the progression schema. **bk scaffolds structure; the agent fills content.** Do NOT have bk author narrative prose.

## Scope
- `bk progression new <topic>`: create a `progression`-labeled bead with a `## Current understanding` placeholder + empty `## Log`, kept off the ready board (see `.5`).
- `bk progression add <id> --type <baseline|deepening|pivot|correction> [message]`: append a dated entry to `## Log`.
- `bk progression list`: list progression beads (cross-project) with their `## Current understanding` one-liner.
- Integrate with `bd` the same way other bk commands do (no `bd create` wrapper for general beads — this is a focused scaffolder for the one structured shape).

## Acceptance
- `bk progression new` produces a bead that passes `beadspec` progression validation.
- `add` appends a correctly-formatted dated entry.
- `list` shows progressions and is consistent with the board-exclusion in `.5`.

## Deps
- Blocked by `.2` (needs the progression schema).
close_reason: Shipped: bk progression new/add/list scaffolder.

title: bk board/ready: exclude progression-labeled beads
description:
# bk board/ready: exclude progression-labeled beads

## Summary
Living-document progression beads must not appear as actionable work. Filter them out of the work surfaces.

## Scope
- In `internal/board` + the ready logic: filter out beads carrying the `progression` label from board, ready, and summary views.
- Make the excluded-label set **configurable** (default `progression`) rather than hard-coding a single string.

## Acceptance
- A `progression`-labeled bead never appears in `bk board` / ready / summary output.
- Non-progression beads are unaffected.
- Tests cover both inclusion and exclusion.

## Deps
- Blocked by `.4` (progression beads exist to exclude; functionally needs the label convention from `.2`).
close_reason: Shipped: board/ready/summary exclusion of progression label.

title: bk hooks: pre-push schema enforcement
description:
# bk hooks: pre-push schema enforcement

## Summary
Hard-gate at push: block landing a bead that violates its type schema (primarily an epic without rationale / a malformed `## Decisions` block). **Reuses the beadspec validation from `.3` — no second implementation.**

## Scope
- Extend `internal/hooks` pre-push to run `beadspec.Validate` over the beads changed in the push range.
- Block by default only on **epic-schema** violations (rationale presence + `## Decisions` shape). Progression findings stay advisory (doctor-only), never push-blockers — do not block living docs.
- Emit a clear failure message naming the offending bead + the violated rule.

## Acceptance
- Pushing an epic with empty rationale, or a decision missing `Why:`, fails the hook with an actionable message.
- A conforming epic passes.
- Tests cover both via the hooks test harness.

## Deps
- Blocked by `.3` (shared validation path).
close_reason: Shipped: bk guard beadspec + pre-push hard gate for epic violations.

title: Adopt rationale/progression convention in consuming repos' AGENTS.md
description:
# Adopt the rationale/progression convention in consuming repos' AGENTS.md

## Summary
Document the two-artifact contract where it is consumed. Short AGENTS.md block in agentflow first, then other active repos. Points at beadspec as the source of truth.

## Scope
- Add an AGENTS.md section stating:
  - Epics carry per-decision rationale in a `## Decisions` block (`Decision: <what> — Why: <rationale>` per entry).
  - Topic arcs get a `progression`-labeled bead with `## Current understanding` + dated `## Log`, kept off the work board.
  - bk `doctor`/`hooks` enforce this from `pkg/beadspec`.
- agentflow first; enumerate follow-on repos.

## Acceptance
- agentflow `AGENTS.md` contains the contract block, consistent with the beadspec seed schemas.

## Deps
- Blocked by `.2` (schema is the source of truth the doc references).
- NOTE: this change **lands in the agentflow repo**, not beekeeper-go.

title: bk: drift guard is push-gated — add commit-time/local drift detection to close the silent-accumulation window
description: Evidence from agentflow (real incident, 2026-06-01): a branch 513 commits behind origin/main accumulated 154 pr-beads regressions (134 dropped-record, 10 status-rewind, 10 stale-timestamp) over 6 days with ZERO signal until a human manually ran bk doctor. Root-cause chain: (1) the bd daemon auto-commits 'bd sync' snapshots at COMMIT time on the stale branch; (2) bk's drift guard (trunk-sync) is PUSH-gated, but the branch had no upstream so nothing was ever pushed -> pre-push guard never fires; (3) the only installed hook that DID fire is bd's pre-commit, which runs 'bd sync --flush-only' and performs no drift check (see .git/hooks/pre-commit lines 1-7,39-44 — pure flush, happily commits a stale snapshot). Net: an unguarded window between manual 'bk doctor' and pre-push where drift originates and compounds locally. FIX DIRECTION: bk install-hooks should offer a pre-commit drift guard (or augment bd's flush hook) that cheaply warns/refuses when the current branch is >N commits behind base, sync.branch is unset, or bd state is needs_manual_sync — converting a silent 6-day drift into a first-commit warning. Consider a 'bk doctor --gate' fast exit-code mode agents can run on repo entry. Partly bd territory: daemon should not silently auto-commit bd-sync on a wildly-behind, upstream-less branch.
close_reason: shipped in 79f5814 — internal/drift + pre-commit drift gate + bk doctor --gate

title: bk doctor: flag when bk guard hooks are not installed (only bd flush hook present)
description: Evidence from agentflow (2026-06-01): the repo had .git/hooks/pre-commit + post-merge, but those are bd's OWN hooks (pre-commit = 'bd sync --flush-only', no drift check), and there was NO pre-push hook — i.e. 'bk install-hooks' was never run. So the only bead protection was manual bk doctor. There is currently no signal that bk's guard hooks are absent; an operator/agent has no way to know they're unprotected. FIX DIRECTION: add a bk doctor check that detects when a bead repo is missing bk's guard hook(s) (distinguishing bk hooks from bd's flush-only pre-commit) and emits a YELLOW with remediation 'bk install-hooks'. Make 'bk install-hooks' idempotent/re-runnable so the remediation is safe to suggest. Pairs with bkg-59b (commit-time drift guard) — bkg-59b adds the guard; this bead makes its absence self-surfacing. Optional: recommend bk install-hooks as part of repo onboarding docs.
close_reason: shipped in 67d0651 — doctor.checkBkHooks + harness goOnlyCheckNames

title: bk lease release hard-fails when .beadkeeper/identity.toml is missing
description: Observed in toolgate-v2 repo. 'bk lease release <id>' errors: 'identity not configured at ./.beadkeeper/identity.toml. Leasing requires a canonical-handle map.' This blocks releasing a stale lease that bk doctor itself flagged. Expected: bk should resolve identity from bk identity / git config, or degrade to a best-effort release with a clear one-line setup hint, rather than hard-blocking. Repro: in a repo without .beadkeeper/identity.toml, run bk doctor (flags stale lease), then bk lease release <id> -> error.
design: AUDIT (read-only, beekeeper-go @754f723): REAL_GAP. lease.ResolveCaller (internal/lease/lease.go:138-144) hard-fails when .beadkeeper/identity.toml is missing, but identity is documented OPT-IN (cmd/bk/identity.go:16-18). cmd/bk/lease.go:62-67 calls ResolveCaller before Release so the AlreadyReleased no-op path (lease.go:244-251) is unreachable; --as handle does not bypass. Actual release mutation (lease.go:265) is 'bd update <id> --status open --assignee empty' which works with a raw handle. FIX (~10 lines): in ResolveCaller, when cfg==nil fall through to RawHandle() (git user.email/BD_ACTOR) instead of erroring; keep 'unknown alias' error only when cfg present. Files: internal/lease/lease.go + lease_test.go (no-config-degrades test).
close_reason: fixed in 6c24bf6 — ResolveCaller degrades to raw handle when identity.toml missing

title: Beekeeper Go — single-binary Go rewrite of beadkeeper (V2)
description: Reimplement beadkeeper (Python, ~5k LOC, zero runtime deps) as a single static Go binary. Motivation: distribution — ship one binary instead of interpreter+venv+pip. Separate repo theaichimera/beekeeper-go, binary 'bk'. Stays a wrapper around git/bd/ps (no reimplementation, no SQLite driver). Behavioral parity with the Python tool is the bar: output, exit codes, refusal conditions. Full spec: docs/handoff/EPIC.md.
acceptance_criteria: All cli.py subcommands have behavior-equivalent Go implementations; 133-equivalent tests green; diff harness shows zero divergence vs Python; brew install works; bk doctor GREEN on a real repo; no secrets/vendor names in code or history.
close_reason: EPIC COMPLETE. v0.1.0 shipped: history scrubbed (0 vendor tokens, verify clean) + force-pushed (c800a5d), repo public, GitHub Release with darwin/linux arm64+x86_64 binaries, homebrew formula published to theaichimera/homebrew-tap. brew chain verified (formula resolves+fetches); binary runs: 'bk 0.1.0'. NOTE: local brew install blocked only by outdated Xcode CLT on this machine (environmental, not a release issue).

title: M0 — Scaffolding & CI
description: Create Go module, cobra skeleton, goreleaser config, GitHub Actions matrix {ubuntu,macos}x{go1.22,1.23}, MIT license, README stub. Binary name 'bk'. CGO_ENABLED=0.
acceptance_criteria: CGO_ENABLED=0 go build yields a runnable binary; 'bk version' works; CI green on both OSes.
close_reason: M0 shipped via PR #1. Commits 3b07f09 (scaffold) + 7f1ca13 (CI cgo fix). CI 26702960651 success on {ubuntu,macos} x {go1.22,1.23} + golangci-lint. https://github.com/theaichimera/beekeeper-go/pull/1

title: M1 — Shared core (git/project/config/filesync/proc)
description: Implement internal/git (os/exec wrapper), internal/project (discovery + daemon/git state), internal/config (TOML+JSON), internal/filesync (cloud root detection), internal/proc (cross-platform ps/PID liveness — HIGHEST RISK, isolate per-OS files with recorded fixtures).
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests for project discovery, git ref/tree helpers, filesync root detection, and proc liveness (stale vs alive PID), validated against fixtures derived from the Python tests.

title: Backlog-hygiene tooling: deterministic bk commands so agents stop hand-rolling bd/jq/git
description:
## Why

During a real review of the `agentflow` backlog (627 beads: 328 closed, 33 in_progress, 266 open), `bk` could answer almost none of the questions an operator/agent actually asks about backlog health. The agent had to hand-roll everything with raw tools:

- status counts / % complete  → `bd list --json | jq 'group_by(.status)'`
- stale-WIP ranking           → `bd list --json | jq` over `updated_at`
- "shipped but never closed"  → `git log origin/main --grep=agentflow-<id>` per bead

That investigation found ~18 of 33 `in_progress` beads were already shipped (each had a merged PR whose title named the bead) but never closed — i.e. real WIP was ~12, not 33. `bk` surfaced none of this.

## Goal

The whole point of `bk` is that an agent should NOT have to go renegade with bespoke `bd`/`jq`/`git` pipelines every time. These should be **deterministic, repeatable, scriptable** commands with `--json` and stable exit codes — the same contract as the existing `guard` family.

`bk` today is strong on infrastructure health (sync, daemons, leases, merge-stomp prevention via `pr-beads`) but has almost nothing for **backlog hygiene**. This epic closes that gap.

## Children

1. `bk board --summary` / `--json` — aggregate counts, % complete, machine-readable board.
2. Stale-WIP detection — flag `in_progress` beads untouched > N days (in `doctor` + board summary).
3. `bk guard stale-beads` — git↔backlog reconciliation: beads that look shipped (id in a merged PR/commit title on the default branch) but are still open/in_progress.

## Principle

Anything an agent currently does to a `.beads/` backlog with raw `jq`/`git` and gets a useful answer is a candidate `bk` command. Determinism + `--json` + exit codes so it can run in CI and in agent loops.
close_reason: epic complete: board summary/json + stale-wip + guard stale-beads all merged

title: bk board --summary / --json (aggregate counts, % complete, machine-readable)
description:
## Problem

`bk board` dumps every ready bead (250+ wrapped lines on agentflow) with no aggregate view and no machine-readable output. To answer "how are we doing?" the agent fell back to `bd list --json | jq`.

## Deliverable

Add an aggregate/summary mode and JSON output to `bk board`.

- `bk board --summary <path>`: human-readable rollup, no per-bead dump:
  - total beads; counts by status (open / in_progress / blocked / closed)
  - % complete (closed / total)
  - active (non-closed) counts by priority (P0..P4)
  - in_progress count + stale-in_progress count (ties into child .2)
- `bk board --json <path>`: machine-readable — the same aggregates PLUS the ready/in_progress/blocked lists, so agents can script against it instead of parsing `bd` output.

## Acceptance criteria

- `bk board --summary` on agentflow prints the rollup (e.g. TOTAL 627 / closed 328 / in_progress 33 / open 266 / 52% complete / P0:3 P1:53 ...) in <1s, no per-bead spam.
- `bk board --json` emits valid JSON with `totals`, `by_status`, `by_priority`, and the lists; deterministic ordering.
- Existing default `bk board` behavior unchanged (back-compat).
- Works across multiple projects when given a parent dir (same discovery as today).
- Exit codes per bk contract; `--json` never interleaves human text.

## Motivating example

agentflow review needed status counts + % complete; `bk board` couldn't provide them — derived via `bd list --json | jq group_by(.status)`.
acceptance_criteria: bk board --summary prints status/priority rollup + % complete with no per-bead dump; bk board --json emits deterministic JSON aggregates+lists; default board unchanged.
close_reason: shipped in #17/#18/#19

title: Stale-WIP detection: flag in_progress beads untouched > N days (doctor + board)
description:
## Problem

Nothing in `bk` flags beads parked in `in_progress` for a long time. agentflow had 33 in_progress, 22 of them untouched for 7+ days (one since 2026-05-06, ~26 days). This WIP bloat is invisible until someone manually ranks `bd list --json` by `updated_at`.

## Deliverable

Stale-WIP detection as a first-class `bk` signal.

- A `bk doctor` check that flags `in_progress` (and optionally `open`/`blocked`) beads whose `updated_at` is older than a threshold.
  - Default threshold: 7 days. Configurable via flag (`--stale-days N`) and/or `.beads/config.json`.
  - Severity: YELLOW (advisory) by default; count surfaced in the project health line, e.g. "pr-wip: 22 in_progress beads stale >7d (oldest 26d: agentflow-6ml)".
- Surface the same count in `bk board --summary` (child .1).

## Acceptance criteria

- `bk doctor` on a repo with stale in_progress beads emits a YELLOW `stale-wip` check naming the count, the threshold, and the oldest offender.
- Threshold configurable; `--stale-days 0` disables the check.
- Timestamp parsing handles real bead `updated_at` values: RFC3339 WITH timezone offsets and fractional seconds (e.g. `2026-05-06T16:50:40.133129+03:00`) — note jq's `fromdateiso8601` chokes on these, so the Go impl must parse offsets properly.
- `--json` output lists offending bead ids + ages.
- Clean repos (no stale WIP) emit no check (silent), consistent with other doctor checks.

## Motivating example

agentflow: 33 in_progress, 22 stale >7d — computed by hand from `updated_at`. `bk` should report this automatically.
acceptance_criteria: bk doctor emits YELLOW stale-wip check (count + threshold + oldest offender); threshold configurable; parses RFC3339 with TZ offset + fractional seconds; --json lists offenders; silent when clean.
close_reason: shipped in #17/#18/#19

title: bk guard stale-beads: git<->backlog reconciliation (shipped-but-not-closed)
description:
## Problem (highest-value gap)

A bead's work often lands (PR merged to the default branch, commit/PR title naming the bead id) but the bead is never moved to `closed`. On agentflow this hid ~18 of 33 `in_progress` beads — real WIP was ~12. Detecting this today means running `git log origin/<default> --grep=<prefix>-<id>` per bead by hand. This is the post-merge analogue of `bk guard pr-beads` (bkg-lrc): pr-beads catches backlog drift GOING INTO a merge; this catches drift that ACCUMULATES after merges.

## Deliverable

`bk guard stale-beads` (a.k.a. backlog reconciliation) — deterministic git↔backlog drift report.

- Derive the bead-id prefix from `.beads/` (e.g. `agentflow-`).
- Scan merged commits on the default branch (`git log <branch> --grep`) for bead-id references in commit/PR titles. (Optionally cross-check merged PR titles via the GitHub API when a token is present; git-log-only must work offline.)
- Report two classes:
  - **shipped-not-closed (RED/YELLOW):** bead in `open`/`in_progress` whose id appears in a merged commit/PR title on the default branch. Include the bead id, status, and the landing commit/PR (sha + subject).
  - **closed-no-landing (advisory):** `closed` bead with no referencing commit — possible mis-close. (Lower severity; behind a flag is fine.)
- Match precision: prefer the id appearing as a delimited token in the SUBJECT (e.g. `agentflow-xymh)` / `(agentflow-xymh)`), not just anywhere in the body, to avoid tangential-reference false positives (the agentflow run saw `4i54` referenced in 8 commits but only some were the actual fix; `afby`/`6ml` were referenced tangentially and were NOT done — the tool must not over-claim).

## Acceptance criteria

- `bk guard stale-beads <path>` lists shipped-not-closed beads with their landing PR/commit. On agentflow it must flag at least: `xymh`#736, `o1b4`#737, `0dh4`/`fz56`#738, `e42f`#777, `1k8x.1`#831, `1k8x.2`#834, `1k8x.5`#836, `1k8x.6`#837, `1k8x.7`#833, `1k8x.9`#839, `4yzw`#841, `p561`#842, `lgd2`#843, `4dll`#844, `h2ml.1`#876.
- Must NOT flag tangential-only references as shipped (e.g. `afby`, `6ml`).
- `--json` output (bead id, status, landing sha/subject/PR#); deterministic ordering.
- Configurable lookback / branch / prefix; exit codes per bk contract (RED => non-zero so it can gate CI).
- Offline mode (git-log only) works without any GitHub token.
- Optional `--fix` is OUT OF SCOPE for v1 (report only) — closing is a human/agent decision; but the JSON should be shaped so an agent can drive `bd close <id> --reason "shipped in #<PR>"` deterministically.

## Motivating example

This exact agentflow run: ~18 in_progress beads already shipped, found via manual `git log --grep`. `bk guard stale-beads` would have produced the same list deterministically in one command.
acceptance_criteria: Flags open/in_progress beads whose id is in a merged commit/PR subject on default branch, with landing PR/commit; must catch the agentflow set (xymh#736..h2ml.1#876) and must NOT flag tangential refs (afby/6ml); --json deterministic; offline git-only works; RED=>nonzero for CI.
close_reason: shipped in #17/#18/#19

title: bk reads stale issues.jsonl after bd mutations (bd export debounce) — add freshness detection to doctor/board/guard
description:
User report: right after `bd update`, `bk guard`/`bk doctor` don't reflect the change until a `bd sync`.

## Confirmed
Empirical: `bd update <id> -d MARKER` -> sqlite has MARKER immediately, `.beads/issues.jsonl` does not (export debounced by bd's daemon). bk has NO daemon and NO cache of its own — every bk run reads `.beads/issues.jsonl` fresh (beadlint.ScanRepo, board, doctor). The "snapshot" is bd's lazy DB->JSONL export, not bk state.

## Why not "build into bd update"
That's a bd-side change (synchronous export per mutation) — bd debounces deliberately (write amplification / commit noise), and bk doesn't own bd. bk should fix the READ side instead.

## Proposed fix, per surface
1. **Shared freshness probe** (internal/beadlint or project): detect JSONL-behind-DB. Cheap heuristic: mtime(beads.db) > mtime(issues.jsonl) (sqlite WAL caveats). Authoritative: compare `bd export` stdout hash vs on-disk JSONL (bd already tracks export_hashes).
2. **bk doctor / bk board**: new check/banner — YELLOW "bead DB has changes not yet exported to issues.jsonl — run `bd sync` (or wait for daemon flush)". Optionally self-heal with explicit flag, never silently mutate the working tree.
3. **bk guard beadspec (pre-push)**: do NOT validate against fresh export — what's pushed is the *committed* JSONL, so blocking on stale content is CORRECT when the rationale fix hasn't been exported+committed. Fix is the message: when lag detected, replace "epic missing rationale" with "your DB has newer bead state than the JSONL being pushed — run `bd sync`, commit, re-push". Current message gaslights a user who just fixed the epic.

Related fidelity gap (separate, note only): guard scans the working-tree JSONL, not the pushed ref's content.
close_reason: fixed: progression argv[0]+rc handling; freshness probe wired into doctor/board/guard

title: doctor hook tests assume git init creates hookless repos — breaks under global init.templateDir

Fails identically on a clean tree. Fix: test helpers should git init with --template= (empty) or set GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR='' so synthetic repos are hermetic. Audit other tests that git init temp repos for the same assumption.

title: bk guard pr-beads — content-aware backlog-regression gate for PRs
description:
## Problem

A feature branch cut from main carries a snapshot of `.beads/issues.jsonl`. While the branch lives, the daemon advances bead state on main. Merging the branch reverts the backlog file — status rewind, assignee loss, dropped records.

Real incident: a branch was cut when bead `.24` was `open`; main advanced it to `in_progress` (assignee `queryparser-agent`); the branch still carried the old file. Merging would silently revert `.24` to `open` and drop the assignee. GitHub flagged mergeability UNKNOWN.

`bk guard sync-branch` does NOT catch this: `_branch_records_subset_of_sync` compares by record **id**, not content, and explicitly assumes "bead edits only ever originate on the sync branch"; it also scans only local `refs/heads`, never an incoming PR.

## Deliverable

`bk guard pr-beads` — diffs bead JSONL between a base and head ref and reports backlog regressions; runnable as a GitHub PR/CI gate.

## Detection (per bead id present in BOTH base and head)

- status rewind: rank open=0, in_progress=1, blocked=1, closed=2; head.rank < base.rank => RED
- assignee loss/overwrite: base assignee set, head clears/changes => RED
- stale timestamp: if updated_at/modified present, head older than base for same id => RED (prefer this signal)
- dropped record: id in base, absent in head => RED
- forward-only (new ids; head strictly newer) => GREEN

## Policies (--policy)

- regression (default): only regressions fail (beads-on-main repos)
- no-beads (strict): ANY `.beads/issues.jsonl` modification in base..head fails (dedicated-sync-branch repos)

## CLI / CI contract

`bk guard pr-beads --base <ref> --head <ref> [--policy regression|no-beads] [--json] [--strict]`
Defaults: base = $GITHUB_BASE_REF or origin/<default>; head = HEAD.
Exit codes (mirror bk): 0 clean | 2 RED regression | 1 generic/--strict-yellow | 64 usage | 127 git missing.
`--json`: findings list {id, field, kind, base_value, head_value}.

## Integration

- bk doctor: opt-in check (skipped unless base ref resolvable)
- bk install-hooks: extend pre-push to optionally run --policy no-beads vs upstream sync branch; reuse hook marker; honor BEADKEEPER_SKIP_HOOK / BEADKEEPER_BLOCK_ON_RED
- docs: README guard section + copy-paste GitHub Actions snippet

## Subtasks

1. internal/prbeads (or internal/guard) detection core + table-driven tests
2. cmd/bk wiring: `guard pr-beads` flags, exit codes, --json
3. base/head ref resolution (merge-base, GITHUB_BASE_REF) in internal/git
4. doctor integration (opt-in) + install-hooks pre-push extension
5. docs: README guard section + GitHub Actions workflow snippet
6. diff-harness parity entry (or documented Go-only divergence in docs/PARITY.md)

## Done when

- The PR #13 scenario (same id, open <- in_progress, assignee dropped) is flagged RED
- A forward-only change (new bead, or open -> in_progress on head) is GREEN
- no-beads policy fails on any `.beads/issues.jsonl` diff
- Runs headless in CI with correct exit codes; GOOS=windows build OK; golangci-lint + go test green on all OSes
acceptance_criteria: PR #13 scenario flagged RED; forward-only changes GREEN; no-beads policy fails on any .beads/issues.jsonl diff; headless CI exit codes correct; GOOS=windows build + lint + tests green on all OSes.
close_reason: Closed

title: progression cmds exec bare subcommand as binary (missing "bd" argv[0]) + ignore bd exit code -> silent no-ops
description:
Bug report (agentflow user, bk 0.5.0, bd 0.47.1, macOS arm64): `bk progression new` prints success/exit 0 but creates nothing; `bk progression list` prints "no progressions." while 5 progression-labeled beads exist.

## Root cause (confirmed by local repro)

Two stacked defects in cmd/bk/progression.go, both shipped in v0.5.0 (bkg-4zi):

1. **Missing "bd" argv[0].** All four BdRun call sites pass the bd subcommand as args[0]:
   - new:  {"create", topic, "-t", "task", "--labels", "progression", "-d", body, "--silent"}
   - add:  {"update", id, "-d", updated}
   - list: {"list", "-l", "progression", "--json"}
   - bdDescription: {"show", id, "--json"}
   execwrap.Run executes args[0] as the binary, so bk literally tries to exec a binary named `create`/`list`/`update`/`show` -> rc=127 (not found). Convention everywhere else (staleship.go, export.go) is []string{"bd", ...}.

2. **rc discarded.** progression.go branches on err, but the execwrap contract says "err is non-nil only when stdout/stderr could not be captured; callers should branch on rc, not err". rc 127 + err nil -> success path -> "created progression : <topic>" with EMPTY id (stdout empty), exit 0. Same for list: empty stdout -> parseBeadList -> nil -> "no progressions.", exit 0.

The empty id in the user's transcript ("created progression : ") was the tell.

## Why tests missed it
progression_test.go covers only pure helpers (newProgressionBody, appendLogEntry, currentUnderstandingOneLiner, parseBeadList). No test exercises the BdRun argv or the rc branch.

## Not bugs
- bd 0.47.1 supports --labels/--silent (create) and -l/--label (list) — flags fine.
- "list exited 1 when piped through non-matching grep" — that was grep's own exit status in the pipeline; bk list exits 0 on the empty case (verified).
- Reporter's env quirks (non-main branch, no-daemon, JSONL hash warning) — red herrings; bd was never invoked at all.

## Fix
- Prepend "bd" in all four call sites (or make a typed helper that owns the argv prefix so this class of bug can't recur).
- Branch on rc != 0: stderr + exit 1.
- Keep printing the bead id on success (code already does; it'll be non-empty once create actually runs).
- Add regression tests injecting a fake BdRunner asserting argv[0]=="bd" and that rc!=0 -> non-zero bk exit.
close_reason: fixed: progression argv[0]+rc handling; freshness probe wired into doctor/board/guard

Related: bkg-8nw.

title: stale-beads v2 hardening: precision + authoritative status + apply mode
description:
## Why

`bk guard stale-beads` (bkg-bqa.3) was dogfooded against the real `agentflow` backlog (48 findings) and then used to close 40 shipped-but-not-closed beads. The exercise surfaced three concrete defects the tool should fix so the WHOLE workflow — detect AND reconcile — is deterministic and an agent never has to hand-run `bd` in a shell loop.

Observed on 2026-06-01:
- 7 of 48 findings (15%) were FALSE POSITIVES: the "landing" commit was the bead's own filing/spec commit, not implementation.
- After `bd close agentflow-l6q` (bd DB = closed), the guard STILL reported l6q as shipped-not-closed, because it reads `.beads/issues.jsonl`, which lags the `bd` SQLite DB.
- Closing the 40 beads was done by hand-running 40 `bd close` commands; one silently missed (write race) and one (agentflow-9wup) was correctly blocked by an open child (agentflow-7ftc) — all handled manually, off-tool.

## Children
1. (P1) Exclude bd-management commits from shipped detection.
2. (P1) Read authoritative bead status, not stale issues.jsonl.
3. (P2) apply/--close mode: deterministic batch close.
close_reason: epic complete

title: stale-beads: exclude bd-management commits (chore(bd|beads): file/update, spec()) from shipped detection
description:
## Problem

`bk guard stale-beads` flags any open/in_progress bead whose id appears in a shipped commit subject. But some subjects NAME a bead without shipping it — they file or spec it. On the agentflow run, 7 of 48 findings (15%) were false positives:

- `spec(agentflow-1k8x): ...` (#830) — spec commit (epic, children still open)
- `chore(bd): file agentflow-5ctm ...` / `... km84 ...` (#1052)
- `chore(bd): file demo-app onboarding bead (agentflow-h2ud) ...` (#1003)
- `chore(bd): file agentflow-znpx ...` (#1009)
- `chore(beads): file agentflow-cazl ...` (#1166)
- `chore(bd): update agentflow-ix5u ...` (#1013)

## Deliverable

In the commit-subject classifier, treat bead-management commits as NON-shipping:
- Conventional-commit type `spec` → never shipping.
- Scope `chore(bd):` / `chore(beads):` (file / update / etc.) → never shipping.
- Only implementation types count as shipped: `feat`, `fix`, `perf`, `refactor` (make this allowlist configurable via flag / config).

## Acceptance criteria

- Re-running on the agentflow-shaped fixture flags ZERO of {1k8x, 5ctm, km84, h2ud, znpx, cazl, ix5u}.
- Still flags every genuine `feat(...)`/`fix(...)` shipped bead from the existing bkg-bqa.3 fixture.
- The implementation-type allowlist and the bd-management exclusions are covered by table-driven tests.
acceptance_criteria: Re-run on agentflow fixture flags 0 of {1k8x,5ctm,km84,h2ud,znpx,cazl,ix5u}; still flags all genuine feat/fix; implementation-type allowlist + bd-management exclusions table-tested.
close_reason: shipped in #20

title: stale-beads: read authoritative bead status (bd DB), not lagging issues.jsonl
description:
## Problem

`bk guard stale-beads` reads bead status from `.beads/issues.jsonl`, which LAGS the authoritative `bd` SQLite DB. Observed on 2026-06-01:

- `bd close agentflow-l6q` → `bd` reported "✓ Closed"; `bd list --json` showed status=closed.
- BUT `.beads/issues.jsonl` on disk still had `"id":"agentflow-l6q" ... "status":"open"`.
- So `bk guard stale-beads` re-reported l6q as shipped-not-closed — a false positive caused purely by read-lag.

The daemon flushes the JSONL asynchronously, so any guard/board command run shortly after a mutation sees stale status.

## Deliverable

Source bead status from an authoritative, fresh read. Options (pick one, document the choice):
- Query `bd` directly (e.g. `bd list --json`) for status instead of parsing issues.jsonl, OR
- Detect the bd DB and read it, OR
- Add a `--refresh` that triggers/awaits a JSONL flush before reading, and document the lag otherwise.

Likely applies to `bk board` too (same JSONL source).

## Acceptance criteria

title: stale-beads: --close/--apply mode (deterministic batch close, skip blocked, dry-run default)
description:
## Problem

`bk guard stale-beads` reports shipped-not-closed beads and emits a `bd_close_command` string per finding, but the agent still has to hand-run them. On 2026-06-01 that meant running 40 `bd close` commands in a shell loop — off-tool. Two things went wrong that a tool should own:
- One close silently missed on first pass (write race when hammering bd 40x); needed a manual retry.
- `agentflow-9wup` could not close — `bd` refused: "blocked by open issues [agentflow-7ftc] (use --force)". Handled manually.

## Deliverable

`bk guard stale-beads --close` (apply mode):
- DRY-RUN by default; require `--apply` to mutate.
- For each GENUINE shipped finding (after the Child .1 bd-management filter and Child .2 authoritative-status read), close it with reason `shipped in #<PR>`.
- Skip beads blocked by open issues (report them with the blocker id, e.g. 9wup←7ftc) unless `--force`.
- Race-safe / idempotent: verify status after each close; re-running is a clean no-op.
- Optional `--exclude <id,...>` to hold specific beads (e.g. a P0 pending verification like agentflow-4i54).
- Print a summary: { closed, skipped_blocked, skipped_excluded, failed }.

## Acceptance criteria

- On the agentflow-shaped fixture, `--apply` closes all genuine shipped beads in ONE command.
- Blocked beads are skipped with a clear blocker reason; `--force` overrides.
- Re-running `--apply` is a no-op (0 closed).
- Without `--apply`, nothing is mutated (dry-run shows the plan).
acceptance_criteria: --apply closes all genuine shipped beads in one command; skips blocked beads (e.g. 9wup<-7ftc) unless --force; re-run is no-op; without --apply nothing mutates.
